EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A strong pressure gradient caused windy to high wind conditions across Southeastern Arizona on January 10th and 11th. A Wind Advisory was in effect from 5 PM on the 10th to 2 PM on January 11th in the mountains and from 5 AM to 2 PM Sunday for much of the valleys. EPISODE_NARRATIVE: An isolated thunderstorm developed during the late afternoon hours on the 30th just south of I-8 near Casa Grande, AZ and steadily moved eastward towards I-10 near Eloy. The thunderstorm was fueled by MLCAPE values near 500 J/KG. With DCAPE values exceeding 1000 J/KG, strong gusty winds was the main hazard with nearby surface observing sites reporting wind gusts exceeding 40 mph. Winds of this magnitude were enough to produce dense blowing dust along I-10 near Toltec Rd, just northwest of Eloy, AZ.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Visibility down as low 50-100 ft in dense blowing dust from thunderstorm winds along I-10 near Toltec Rd. This resulted in cars pulling off to the side of the road on I-10. No accidents nor injuries were reported.

The fire was able to spread along a riverbed, jumping U.S. Highway 60 (the main highway corridor connecting Phoenix and Las Vegas). The fire was able to be fully contained approximately 100 hours after its initial start with a total of 84 acres burned. At the end, the blaze destroyed approximately eleven RVs, seven vehicles, two trailers, and two outbuildings with 25 people displaced. The fire also damaged some electrical equipment causing a power outage with approximately 176 customers affected. In total, the fire consumed nearly 84 acres. No injuries were reported.
